nodes.label: Receptionist
nodes.rationale: A cluster-wide service registry: every node hosts one, registrations are locally authoritative and peers learn foreign ones via gossip. The most flexible discovery, paid for in gossip cost — static routing is cheaper with a ClusterRouter. Started with null instead of a cluster it works locally only, useful for tests and single-node apps.

nodes.label: ServiceKey
nodes.rationale: A string identifier plus a message type parameter, so a Listing carries refs typed as ActorRef<T>. Keys are values — define once, import everywhere. Two keys with the same id are the same key at runtime; the type parameter is compile-time only, so mixing types under one id is a bug.

nodes.label: Register
nodes.rationale: Adds the ref to the local map and gossips the addition; an optional replyTo yields a Registered acknowledgment. N workers registering under one key is the common pattern — consumers see the whole pool and route as they like.

nodes.label: Find
nodes.rationale: A one-shot lookup answered with a single Listing to the named replyTo, combining local registrations with gossiped remote ones. It carries the current view, not a synchronous cluster query, so registrations not yet gossiped are missing — convergence takes a gossip round or two.

nodes.label: Listing
nodes.rationale: Can carry a stale ref: if a registration was just deregistered elsewhere and the gossip has not propagated, the tell lands silently in dead letters. For high-value operations watch the ref and react to Terminated.

nodes.label: ReceptionistSubscribe
nodes.rationale: Continuous: a fresh Listing now and again on every change, local or gossiped, including node departures — the tool for dynamic routing. Exported under the aliased name because the unqualified Subscribe belongs to DistributedPubSub.

nodes.label: ReceptionistSubscribeRejected
nodes.rationale: Over-limit subscribes are rejected, not dropped: replyTo gets this instead of the first Listing and no listings follow. It matters because a silently dropped Subscribe is indistinguishable from a key that simply has no registrations yet.

nodes.label: Subscription bounds and death watch
nodes.rationale: Two mechanisms keep the subscriber set bounded: the Receptionist death-watches every subscriber so a crash or forgotten cleanup frees the slot on Terminated, and two caps limit the living ones. maxSubscribersPerKey counts subscribers on one key; maxSubscriptionsTotal counts key/subscriber PAIRS across all keys — pairs are what bound memory, since nothing limits how many keys one subscriber may hold.

nodes.label: Registrations are not watched
nodes.rationale: A registration outlives the actor until Deregister is sent or its node leaves, so a Find can return a ref to a stopped actor — guard on the consumer side. Subscribers, by contrast, ARE watched.

nodes.label: MemberRemoved auto-cleanup
nodes.rationale: Covers the 'node crashed with no chance to deregister' case: every registration that node contributed is forgotten and subscribers fire with the smaller listing.
